resources.string: Shizuku or Shevery is required for background autostart management without root.
Autostart allows applications to automatically initialize background services and sync notifications when your device boots up. Manage permissions for each application below.
Showing real receiver state. Flip a switch to change autostart.
Allow access to read and change boot receivers.
Shizuku isn\'t running, so some boot receivers may be hidden and switches are locked.

Allowed - the app's boot receivers are enabled, so Android wakes it after a reboot. Notifications and widgets work immediately, at the cost of a slower, hotter boot.

Not Allowed - its boot receivers are disabled in the package manager. The app stays dead (0 RAM, 0 CPU) until you open it, and sends no notifications until then.

Keep Allowed: alarm clocks, your main messengers, smartwatch companions, health monitors. Safe to block: shopping, social, games and one-off utilities.

Realme UI / ColorOS: com.oplus.safecenter can still drop boot broadcasts for apps that are off in its own Auto-launch list. If an Allowed app doesn't start after reboot, turn it on there too (menu → Realme Auto-launch).

Apps you force-stopped never receive boot broadcasts until opened once.

Autostart is only about starting after reboot. How an app is treated while running is Battery Mode Checker's job.
